02 / KNOW YOUR CLOTH

A fabric with
a past. A future.

A textile shaped by people, process and purpose. Here's where Khadi comes from—and where it can go next.

THEN / THE HISTORY

A cloth of self-reliance.

Khadi became a symbol of India's Swadeshi movement and the idea of self-reliance. The charkha represented local production, dignity of labour and freedom through everyday choices.

NOW / THE PRESENT

Craft in contemporary life.

Today, Khadi connects spinners, weavers, designers and consumers. Its next chapter depends on quality, fresh design and making the craft relevant to how people dress now.

NEXT / THE FUTURE

Made for what comes next.

New silhouettes, thoughtful sourcing and direct relationships with makers can take Khadi into contemporary wardrobes—without losing the handwork that makes it distinctive.

FIRST, WHAT MAKES IT KHADI?

Khadi is the process, not a fibre.

Khadi is fabric made from yarn that is hand-spun and then handwoven. The word describes how the yarn and cloth are made; it does not name one single raw material. Depending on the fibre used, Khadi can have different textures, weights, warmth and drape. That is why the same craft can lead to a light shirt, a textured tee, a warm layer or a refined statement piece. For KHAAS, this opens up a design vocabulary rather than limiting us to one look.

FOUR MATERIAL DIRECTIONS / ONE MAKING TRADITION
01 / BREATHABLE

Cotton Khadi

Hand-spun cotton yarn, handwoven into a breathable fabric with a tactile, natural surface. A versatile direction for tees, shirts, shorts and relaxed everyday pieces.

02 / FINE WEAVE

Muslin Khadi

Fine, lightweight cotton Khadi with an airy feel and softer drape. Muslin describes a fine, lightweight weave or cloth, not a separate fibre. It can work for fluid shirts and layering.

03 / REFINED

Silk Khadi

Khadi made using hand-spun silk yarn and handwoven into a textile with natural texture and subtle lustre. A direction for elevated shirts, special pieces and limited editions.

04 / WARM LAYER

Wool Khadi

Khadi made using hand-spun wool yarn and handwoven into a warmer textile. Its texture and insulation make it a potential choice for overshirts, outerwear and seasonal accessories.

WHY KHADI IS AT THE HEART OF KHAAS

Four material directions. One distinctive way of making.

Cotton, muslin, silk and wool describe different fibres, cloth qualities or fabric directions. Khadi adds another layer: the human process of hand-spinning and hand-weaving. It brings visible texture, variation and a connection to the people who make the cloth. That is the point of difference we want to build into KHAAS—not simply a label that says “natural”, but a design-led brand that values how its material comes into being. Where a product is described as Khadi, its fibre, production process and applicable certification will be verified and stated accurately.

MATERIAL NOTE: The exact fibre, weave, weight and Khadi status will be listed product by product. Muslin is a fine cloth description, not a fibre category. Blended textiles will be clearly identified and will not be presented as pure Khadi.

04 / The process

From fibre
to form.

Good design should respect the people and processes behind the material. Here is the sourcing model we are building towards.

Step 01 / Source

Know the maker.

Work with verified Khadi institutions and artisan producer groups. Confirm fibre, spinning, weaving, provenance and applicable certification before a fabric enters a collection.

Step 02 / Design

Respect the material.

Develop silhouettes around the cloth's real weight, drape, texture and performance. Test samples, shrinkage, colourfastness and construction before production.

Step 03 / Make

Build relationships.

Plan repeat orders, clear payment terms and transparent product information. Credit the producer communities involved, with their agreement.
